newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Danubius sets no div on '96 profits.
newsitem.headline: Danubius sets no div on '96 profits.

text.p: Hungarian hotel chain Danubius voted at its annual meeting on Tuesday to distribute no dividends on 1996 profits, over protests from minority shareholders.

"Usually when you retain or withhold profit it means that you don't eat your golden egg," president and chief executive officer Sandor Betegh told shareholders attending the meeting in a Budapest congress hall.

The board's recommendation not to distribute 1.920 billion forints of after-tax profits on sales of more than nine billion forints was approved by 98 percent of voting capital in attendance, with less than one percent voting against.

Danubius also withheld its 1995 dividend, choosing instead to plough the money back into the company's hotel properties, which were expanded by its 8.125 billion forint purchase of the Hungaria Szalloda Rt hotel chain late last year.

Several stockholders said they objected to the non-payment of dividends when the company was providing discounts to employees using hotel facilities and spent 50 million forints a year sponsoring a sports team.
"It seems like the general tendency is to want to squeeze out the small individuals," one woman said.
Other stockholders said the failure to pay dividends hurt the company's image on international markets.

But Betegh said the growth in value of the stock, which in 1996 rose to more than 4,000 forints from 1,200, and traded on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Tuesday at 5,750 forints, more than compensated.
"Usually when you invest in a company it means that you have trust in the company," Betegh said.

"You must remember that we have institutional investors as well who hold 46 percent of the equity -- they are real professionals and they know exactly where the tendency lies. If a company uses resources in a responsible manner then the market will respond to that."
